chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who was sitting with a group of people and he died while with them, or a man was found among a tribe, or at the door of a people's house, and it was claimed against them (that they were responsible for his death), he said: 'There is nothing upon them, and his blood is not invalidated (i.e., no blood money is due).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on blood money if a person dies while sitting with a group or is found dead among them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'presumption of innocence' (istishab) in cases of ambiguous death, ruling that the burden of proof lies with the claimant to establish liability for blood money (diyah). It clarifies that mere presence or proximity—such as sitting with a group or being found at a doorway—does not automatically incur financial responsibility, protecting individuals from unjust claims without concrete evidence of causation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding a man who was seated with a group of people, so he died and he was with them, or a man was found (dead) among his tribe, or upon a door of a people, so it was claimed against them. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing upon them, nor would his blood be invalidated’.
